input.text: s1 (Given): (V, <.,.>) is a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space with <.,.> antilinear in the first argument, linear in the second, and positive definite (<v, v> > 0 for v != 0), and H = H^dagger satisfies <H u, v> = <u, H v> for all u, v in V.

s2 (Reality of eigenvalues): Let H v = lambda v with v != 0. Then lambda <v, v> = <v, lambda v> = <v, H v> = <H v, v> = <lambda v, v> = conj(lambda) <v, v>. Since v != 0 implies <v, v> > 0, (lambda - conj(lambda)) = 0, so lambda = conj(lambda) is real.

s3 (Orthogonality): Let H u = lambda u and H v = mu v with u != 0, v != 0, and lambda != mu. By s2 both lambda and mu are real, so mu <u, v> = <u, H v> = <H u, v> = conj(lambda) <u, v> = lambda <u, v>. Hence (mu - lambda) <u, v> = 0, and since lambda != mu we conclude <u, v> = 0.

content.text: For any Hermitian operator H = H^dagger on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space (V, <.,.>), every eigenvalue lambda is real (lambda = conj(lambda)) and eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues lambda != mu are orthogonal (<u, v> = 0).
